# Draft:Acharya Pandit Chetan Tiwari

----
Acharya Pandit Chetan Tiwari (born 23 April 2001) is an Indian Hindu priest and practitioner associated with Baglamukhi Tantra and traditional Vedic ritual practices. He is known for his training in Vedic scriptures, Tantric texts, and ritual disciplines studied under the guru–parampara system in Ujjain and Kashi. His work primarily involves conducting traditional ceremonies, following established ritual frameworks, and participating in practices connected with Hindu spiritual centres in Madhya Pradesh and other regions of India.
Early life and background
Chetan Tiwari was born in Barod, Agar district, Madhya Pradesh, India, into a Brahmin family involved in religious and devotional activities. His early exposure to ritual traditions and scriptural teachings came through his father, who participated in religious discourse and related practices. This environment contributed to his interest in Hindu ritual systems and foundational concepts of Sanatan Dharma.
In 2008, he moved to Ujjain, a city historically regarded as an important centre for Vedic and Tantric studies. There he undertook instruction in the Vedas, Upanishads, Shastras, Karma-kanda, and introductory Tantric concepts under the guidance of established teachers connected with local spiritual institutions.
Education and training
From 2016 to 2020, Tiwari pursued further study in Kashi (Varanasi), focusing on advanced scriptural literature, ritual systems, and esoteric traditions associated with Tantric practice. His studies included textual learning, observance of traditional practices, and participation in rituals conducted at various Hindu sites.
During this period, he visited several notable Shaktipeethas and traditional centres of Tantric practice, including Kamakhya, where he engaged in sadhana as part of his extended training.
Work and activities
Following his training, Tiwari became involved in performing rituals and ceremonies associated with Baglamukhi traditions and other classical Hindu practices. His work is centred in Ujjain and includes conducting rites based on established liturgical frameworks, providing ritual services to devotees, and continuing study within his lineage. His practice is rooted in traditional textual interpretations and methodologies maintained through the guru-parampara system.
